PullRequest.Title: chat input: refactor and responsiveness
PullRequest.Body:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call path, repeated clone/attach/geometry mechanism, two-lane layout callers, and observer triggers are explicit in the added code. Exact milliseconds vary by picker count and DOM complexity, which is reflected in medium severity rather than uncertainty about the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: DOM subtree clones, style/layout resolution, and main-thread CPU
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N visible pickers, the loop invokes `_fitsAvailableWidth` up to N times; every invocation clones the full lane, attaches it to the live document, measures each item, and then measures the live lane again. The work therefore grows roughly with N times the lane subtree/geometry work, and is repeated for both primary and secondary lanes on each layout or observed mutation.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased synchronous layout latency and dropped frames while resizing or changing chat picker state
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, picker compactness came from a width observable or CSS container queries; chat input layout did not clone and synchronously measure each picker lane once per candidate item.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added responsive loop tests each progressively compacted state by calling a helper that rebuilds an offscreen clone in the live document and forces geometry reads, and ChatInputPart/NewChatInput invoke this controller from their layout paths while ResizeObserver and MutationObserver can invoke it again.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 87 places `_fitsAvailableWidth(availableWidth)` inside `for (const item of items)`; the newly added helper it reaches performs `cloneNode(true)`, appends the clone to the live parent, and synchronously reads geometry before the next item iteration.
Findings.Title: Measure the picker lane once per responsive pass
Findings.Impact: Dragging the sidebar/editor boundary or changing picker/menu state with several chat controls can perform multiple full subtree clones and forced layouts per lane per update, blocking the UI thread and making the composer visibly janky.
Findings.Evidence: At line 87 the per-item loop calls `_fitsAvailableWidth`; that method calls `_measurePreferredLayout`, which clones `_element`, appends the clone to the live parent, and reads `getBoundingClientRect()` for the clone and every item, followed by live-lane geometry reads. `ChatInputPart.layout` calls two such controllers, and `NewChatInput.layout` also calls two, in addition to each controller's ResizeObserver and subtree MutationObserver. Agent-host sessions can expose multiple core and provider config pickers plus generic chips, so the narrow-width path realistically reaches several iterations.
Findings.Recommendation: Build/reuse one measurement representation per `layout()` (or cache expanded/compact intrinsic widths until a picker-content mutation), derive the progressive fit decisions from those measurements, and coalesce observer/host layout requests so unchanged width/content does not repeat the pass.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize the regular chat composer/sidebar with primary and secondary picker lanes visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `ChatWidget.layout` synchronously calls `ChatInputPart.layout`, which now runs both responsive controllers before layout returns and the next frame can paint.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Progressively compact each item while cloning the complete lane into the live DOM and forcing clone/live geometry resolution for each fit attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to N clone-and-measure operations for N visible items per lane, with two lanes invoked by one `ChatInputPart.layout`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Compact state was derived from a width threshold or CSS container query; host layout did not clone and measure the lane per candidate item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous and blocks the resize/layout frame.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective cardinality is the visible primary/secondary picker count after menu context filtering, including agent-host config pickers and generic chips; each lane can contain several items, and a narrow lane exercises up to one fit attempt per item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All DOM writes, subtree cloning, toolbar relayouts, and geometry reads are serialized on the UI thread. Explicit host layout and separate ResizeObserver delivery are not coalesced by the controller.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no width/content result cache. Warm layouts at the same dimensions repeat compaction, toolbar relayout, cloning, and geometry measurement; MutationObserver disconnection only prevents self-generated mutations from recursively scheduling the same pass.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the loop, clone/attach, geometry reads, and synchronous two-lane callers are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame cost depends on visible picker count, DOM depth, browser, and resize cadence; several context-gated pickers plus generic chips make multiple iterations realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity synchronous repeated layout work; one finding submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize or lay out the new-session composer in the Agents window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `NewChatWidget.layout`/`NewChatInSessionWidget.layout` synchronously call `NewChatInputWidget.layout`, which lays out the editor and then both newly added picker controllers before returning.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke two responsive controllers, each reaching live-DOM clone and geometry measurement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two controller calls per host layout; within each controller up to N clone/measure attempts for N visible pickers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The model picker used a scalar width comparison and the bottom row relied on CSS container queries, without JavaScript subtree cloning.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks composer layout and the next rendered frame.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible config-toolbar actions plus labeled controls in the bottom container; the secondary item collector recursively traverses that container each time it is queried, while fit attempts scale with visible labeled pickers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized UI-thread work. The explicit layout calls and each controller's ResizeObserver can both schedule work; there is no controller-level request coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cached intrinsic picker widths or unchanged-layout fast path; repeated warm layouts rebuild measurements.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The Agents-window control count varies by provider/session configuration, but the synchronous mechanism is present whenever the controllers have visible items.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the submitted repeated-measurement finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Picker labels, menus, or generic agent-host config chips change while the chat input is visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new subtree MutationObserver calls `layout`; its synchronous DOM measurement must finish before the browser can paint the updated picker state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Observe the picker subtree and synchronously recompute responsive state on mutation delivery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full responsive pass per delivered mutation batch per affected lane, with up to N live clone/measure operations inside the pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: CSS container queries handled responsive label presentation without a JavaScript mutation-triggered measurement pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before the updated UI can settle and paint.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One observer callback per mutation delivery batch, multiplied by the visible picker count during progressive fit checks. Generic configuration schemas can add multiple compactable chips.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mutation records are browser-batched, but the callback performs all work synchronously; ResizeObserver and explicit toolbar/host relayout paths are separate and not deduplicated.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Every observed class/style/hidden/text/child mutation invalidates implicitly and triggers a full pass; there is no positive cache for unchanged intrinsic widths or available width.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the callback and work; event frequency is workload-dependent.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Picker-state mutations are less frequent than streamed response text because the observer is scoped to the lane, but menu/context/provider updates are normal product events.
Scenarios.Verdict: Same reportable mechanism as the submitted finding; no duplicate finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a picker after its action moved into toolbar overflow
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click schedules a zero-delay callback, creates/renders a temporary picker view item, and opens it anchored to the overflow button; this is user-triggered rather than on a continuous render path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and render an overflow-specific action view item on demand.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per overflow picker activation, with one retained temporary instance at a time.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Overflow actions invoked the original action and did not create an overflow-specific picker view item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the click-to-open path but bounded and not collection-scaling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One temporary picker instance per user activation. `MutableDisposable` replaces and disposes the previous temporary item, so retained cardinality is bounded to one per chat input (and one automation isolation item in its host).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One scheduled callback per click; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation was introduced on this path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is relevant; picker instances are intentionally recreated only when an overflow action is activated and prior instances are disposed on replacement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Individual picker constructors differ, but the changed lifecycle is bounded and activation-driven.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent performance finding: creation is lazy, one-shot, and replacement disposal bounds retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Responsive SCM repository and integrated-browser toolbars relayout
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Their existing ResizeObservers synchronously call the shared `ToolBar.updateActions`, which now checks computed `display` state while calculating responsive widths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read computed display style for action elements during responsive width calculations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(N) on fitting passes and potentially repeated scans while overflowing; N is the effective toolbar action count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Responsive calculations used action counts/indexes without computed-display reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds style-resolution work to resize/menu updates.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible toolbar action count after menu/context filtering; production toolbars generally contain a small number of actions, though the hide loop can rescan remaining actions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread style queries during each toolbar relayout; browser resize notifications are delivered per observed toolbar.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Visibility is not cached across a pass, but action sets are small and relayout already measured item widths before this change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for added work, insufficient for material impact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No evidence that realistic SCM or browser toolbar action counts make the added scans independently user-visible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: bounded action counts and lack of evidence for a concrete user-visible regression do not meet the reporting threshold.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 33 changed files. Submitted one medium-severity finding for per-picker live-DOM cloning and forced layout on synchronous chat layout/observer paths. Checked overflow picker lifecycle, shared toolbar relayout, caches/coalescing, and all transitive subprocess/IPC/filesystem/database/network boundaries; no additional high-confidence performance regression or regression-fix learning signal was established.
